data.title: Canada to Allow Pension-Fund Investment in Country's Big Airports — Update
data.description:
By Paul Vieira

OTTAWA--Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Tuesday the government is ready to strike deals to hand over operations of the country's four largest airports to institutional investors.

Money raised would be deployed to help build key infrastructure, like new trade corridors, that the country needs, Carney said, as he attempts to reorient the economy and reduce reliance on a protectionist U.S.

In March of last year, Canada said it would open the door to private-sector investment in airports. At present, current rules governing airports have largely prevented private investment in the country's air terminals.

"Canadian pension funds already invest successfully in many airports around the world. It is time to bring that same expertise home to more directly benefit all Canadians," said Carney, unveiling the news at an investment summit he's hosting in Toronto. Among Canada's big pension funds with stakes in foreign airports are Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan, CPP Investment Board and Public Sector Pension Investment Board.

The deals, Carney said, would be set up as long-term concessions, which are agreements under which the private-sector investor handles the operation and maintenance of the airport for a set period. According to Statistics Canada, the country's airports served 158.9 million passengers last year. Toronto's Pearson International is by far the largest, accounting for about 30% of passenger traffic, followed by Vancouver with 16%.

At present, airport authorities are funded through fees paid by users, from air carriers to passengers. Officials had previously said this funding model was in need of change in order to accommodate necessary expansions.

After his speech, Carney said in a question-and-answer session that the policy change on airports is an effort to get Canada's big pension funds to allocate more of their capital domestically. Pension funds have "been exporting, if you will, expertise and capital, to the benefit" of plan members, the prime minister said. "It's been the right thing to do, but we want to get some of that benefit coming back."

data.title: Axon Enterprise Shares Drop After Plan to Offer $1 Billion of 0% Senior Notes
data.description:
By Chris Wack

Axon Enterprise shares were lower after the company said it intends to offer $1 billion of 0% convertible senior notes due 2031 in a public offering.

The stock was down 10%, at $438.87, in morning trade, and is down 42% in the past 12 months.

Axon said it expects to grant the underwriters of the notes an option to buy for settlement within an 11-day period beginning on, and including, the first date on which the notes are issued, up to an additional $150 million of notes, solely to cover over-allotments, if any.

The company said it intends to use a portion of the proceeds of the offering for general corporate purposes, which may include, among other things, providing capital to support Axon's growth and to acquire or invest in product lines, products, services or technologies, including through acquisitions of, or investments in, other businesses.

The notes will mature Sept. 15, 2031, unless earlier converted, redeemed or repurchased. The notes will be senior, unsecured obligations of Axon and will not bear regular interest, and the principal amount of the notes will not accrete.

Write to Chris Wack at chris.wack@wsj.com

data.title: GISEC 2026: Genians Introduces ‘Pinpoint Security Operations’ to Advance Sovereign Cybersecurity
data.description:
Genians, a global leader in Network Access Control (NAC), will unveil the Genians Security Platform (GSP) at GISEC Global 2026, taking place September 16–18 in Dubai. Genians will exhibit with RAS Infotech, its strategic cybersecurity partner in the Middle East, at Stand H8-E130. GISEC Global brings together cybersecurity leaders across government, finance, energy, manufacturing, telecommunications, critical infrastructure, and other sectors from the Middle East, Africa, Asia, Europe, and the Americas.

“As environments become more complex, the fundamentals of cybersecurity need to become clearer,” said Kyeyeon Kim, CTO and Co-Founder of Genians. “Security starts with knowing who and what is connecting, understanding the risk, and turning that decision into the right action. Effective integration must connect visibility, context, and enforcement.”

For 21 years, Genians has focused on identifying and controlling devices at the point of network connection. That foundation has expanded into Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) for access and session control and Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) for endpoint security. GSP brings these capabilities and operational experience into a unified security operations service.

‘Pinpoint Security Operations’: From Detection to Action

Security teams already operate firewalls, VPNs, SIEM, DLP, endpoint security, and other IT systems. The challenge is no longer simply collecting more data. It is identifying what matters and acting on it quickly. GSP works with the security stack organizations already have. It combines distributed data and events, identifies signals that require action, and connects those decisions to enforcement points including NAC, ZTNA, and EDR. Depending on the risk, devices and sessions can be blocked, quarantined, or given restricted access. The goal is simple: turn fragmented security data into decisions, and decisions into enforceable action. Genians calls this approach Pinpoint Security Operations.

Nexus Framework: The Foundation for GSP

GSP runs on the Nexus Framework, which provides common capabilities including identity and access management, tenant and role controls, a shared data lake, workflow automation, monitoring, and AI services. Existing security products can connect through logs, APIs, and database integrations without being rebuilt. This allows GSP to bring Genians and third-party security data into a common environment for analysis and automation.

At GISEC Global, Kim will demonstrate GSP security operations scenarios and the underlying Nexus Framework architecture. The Nexus Framework was developed through a South Korean government-backed international cybersecurity R&D initiative led by KISIA. Genians plans to expand the ecosystem to include additional security technologies and create a practical path for proven cybersecurity solutions to reach global markets.

From Operational Control to Sovereign Cybersecurity

Deployed within the customer's own environment, including air-gapped networks, GSP keeps security data, policies, and response decisions under the organization's control. The direction follows Genians' participation in the Republic of Korea's Presidential Strategic Meeting on New National Security Initiatives in June, where the company proposed building certified cyber defense into national defense exports.

Genians serves more than 5,000 organizations worldwide. Recent expansion includes a UAE insurer adopting both ZTNA and EDR, a new NAC deployment with an India-based organization supporting projects in Africa, and a new local presence in Indonesia.

"Cybersecurity innovation is moving faster than ever, but operational control remains fundamental," said Dong-Bum Lee, CEO of Genians. "With GSP and the Nexus Framework, we are extending 21 years of real-world enforcement experience into an ecosystem where different security technologies can work together while organizations retain control over their data, policies, and response."

About Genians

Genians (KOSDAQ: 263860) secures networks through its NAC, ZTNA, and EDR platforms, delivering the device visibility and control required for both security operations and regulatory compliance. Founded in 2005, Genians is South Korea's No. 1 in NAC and in public-procurement EDR, protecting more than 5,000 customers worldwide across defense, government, finance, and manufacturing. Gartner recognizes Genians as a Representative Vendor. With the industry's first cloud-managed NAC and NAC-driven ZTNA, and now the Genians Security Platform (GSP) for unified security operations, Genians makes these once costly, complex technologies accessible to organizations of every size and to the MSPs and MSSPs that deliver them as a service. For more information, visit www.genians.com.

data.title: OpenAI is working with Anthropic, Google on AI safety, Bloomberg News reports
data.description:
OpenAI is working with rivals Anthropic and Alphabet's Google DeepMind on AI safety, Bloomberg News reported on Tuesday, citing the ChatGPT maker's global policy chief Chris Lehane.

Global concerns about AI's existential risks have risen after the heads of America's leading AI labs came together in a show of unity over the weekend to call for a pause in the development of the technology.

Lehane said OpenAI had been in talks with Anthropic and Google for several weeks and did not believe the three AI firms needed an antitrust waiver to coordinate on safety issues, according to the report.

"It's better to try to work together to prioritize safety," Lehane said at a briefing in Washington, according to Bloomberg News.

In Washington to meet lawmakers, Lehane said OpenAI would support any bipartisan legislation aimed at mitigating catastrophic AI risks, according to the report.

OpenAI, Alphabet and Anthropic did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. Reuters could not independently verify the report.

data.title: IHCL signs SeleQtions hotel in Athirapilly, Kerala
data.description:
The 100-key hotel will be developed in two phases, strengthening IHCL’s presence in the state’s leisure market

Indian Hotels Company (IHCL) has signed a SeleQtions hotel in Athirapilly, Kerala, as a conversion and expansion project. The 100-key hotel will be developed in two phases, strengthening IHCL’s presence in the state’s leisure market.

The first phase will comprise 37 existing operational keys, with the remaining inventory to be added as part of the expansion. The hotel will feature an all-day dining restaurant, a wine and beer lounge and a rooftop dining experience. Facilities for meetings and social gatherings will include banquet venues and meeting rooms, while recreational offerings will comprise a swimming pool, fitness centre and spa with multiple treatment rooms.

Suma Venkatesh, Executive Vice President - Real Estate & Development, IHCL, said, “Kerala continues to be a key leisure market with its diverse tourism offerings and strong connectivity. Athirapilly, with its proximity to the iconic Athirapilly Falls and easy access from Kochi, presents an attractive opportunity to further strengthen our presence in the state. The signing is in line with our focus on expanding our portfolio across distinctive leisure destinations. We are delighted to partner with the Kshema Group for this project and bring the SeleQtions experience to Athirapilly.”

Located in Thrissur district on the banks of the Chalakudy River, the hotel is adjacent to Athirapilly Falls, Kerala’s largest waterfall. It is also in proximity to Cochin International Airport and forms part of leisure itineraries connecting Kochi and Munnar.

Abhinand Basant, Director, Kshema Group, said, “We are delighted to partner with IHCL to bring the SeleQtions brand to Athirappilly. This partnership is an important milestone in our hospitality journey and reflects our commitment to developing distinctive destinations that are deeply connected to their location and surroundings. We look forward to working closely with IHCL to create a memorable hospitality experience in Athirappilly and contribute to the region’s growing tourism potential.”

data.title: Embassy Bets 90% Of Bengaluru Pipeline On North Bengaluru
data.description:
EDL says about 90% of current Bengaluru residential pipeline is concentrated in the north as affluent buyers increasingly seek larger homes, green spaces and airport connectivity

Embassy Developments Ltd (EDL) is concentrating a large part of its Bengaluru residential pipeline in the city’s north, betting on the region’s airport connectivity, expanding commercial infrastructure and demand for larger, premium homes.

The developer plans to launch about Rs 10,000 crore of projects across India by March 2027, with Bengaluru expected to account for about 75 per cent of that pipeline. Within Bengaluru, Managing Director Aditya Virwani said roughly 90 per cent of Embassy’s current pipeline is in the northern part of the city.

North Bengaluru Becomes A Core Growth Market

Embassy’s latest bet on the region is an 85-acre residential development, Embassy Origins, on Chaprakal Road in North Bengaluru. The first phase, comprising Embassy Riverine and Embassy South Reserve, has a combined gross development value of about Rs 4,500 crore.

The development comes as Embassy expands an existing residential footprint in the region. In November 2025, Embassy Developments announced six residential projects in North Bengaluru with a combined launch value of about Rs 10,300 crore and development potential of roughly 5.6 million sq ft.

Virwani said the northern Bengaluru market has been supported by the international airport, commercial developments and expanding residential options, including plotted developments, integrated townships and villas. He said the region now accounts for a significant share of Bengaluru’s residential real estate sales, although the company’s estimate of 35 to 40 per cent was not independently established during the discussion.

The company’s strategy also indicates a broader shift in what affluent buyers are seeking from residential developments. Virwani said buyers are becoming more location-agnostic and increasingly evaluating communities based on factors such as capital appreciation, walkability, lower density and green spaces rather than proximity to the traditional central business districts.

Luxury Demand Supports Premium Projects

Embassy is targeting this demand across different price points, from premium apartments to large-format villas. At Embassy Origins, villas start at about Rs 14 crore, while apartments are priced at more than Rs 2 crore.

The company said its luxury residential customer base includes entrepreneurs, business owners and high-net-worth individuals, with founders of unicorn startups accounting for about one-fourth of the clientele it is seeing in the Rs 10 crore-plus segment.

Embassy also cited CRE Matrix data showing Rs 2,087 crore of Bengaluru home sales above Rs 10 crore last year, of which Rs 1,346 crore was attributed to Embassy projects. These figures were presented by the company during the discussion and were not independently verified.

The developer is also seeing interest from non-resident Indians (NRIs) in markets including Singapore, Dubai and the UAE as its NRI contribution. Reeza Sabatin, Chief Revenue Officer, said historically around 6 per cent to 8 per cent has recently moved to 8 per cent to 10 per cent.

Airport Connectivity Drives The North

The international airport remains a key anchor for North Bengaluru’s residential expansion, according to Embassy. The company expects the region’s appeal to strengthen further as commercial activity, schools, retail, restaurants and public transport infrastructure expand.

Virwani said the company remains bullish on the north even as it evaluates opportunities in East Bengaluru, which currently benefits from established IT corridors and stronger employment-linked demand. The northern market, he said, offers a larger canvas for villas and other space-intensive residential formats.

The developer’s wider launch strategy reinforces the importance of Bengaluru to its growth plans. Embassy said it has about Rs 50,000 crore of GDV across its national portfolio, launched roughly Rs 22,000 crore in the preceding 12 months and plans to launch another Rs 10,000 crore by March 2027. Bengaluru is expected to represent about 75 per cent of that near-term launch value.

Differentiation Becomes Part Of The Strategy

Embassy is positioning Embassy Origins around what it calls “Natural Intelligence”, using the site’s natural contours, water systems and landscape as part of the development rather than treating them as conventional landscaping elements.The project incorporates seven lakes and a stream system, while the company plans to retain natural earth and introduce native vegetation.

Virwani said he was surprised by the demand for the project, although the company had yet to begin formal sales at the time of the discussion. He also cautioned against assigning a specific price premium to the Natural Intelligence concept.

For Embassy, the strategy is therefore not limited to selling homes in a new growth corridor. The company is using North Bengaluru’s expanding infrastructure and available land to build a portfolio spanning premium apartments, villas and integrated communities, while seeking to differentiate those projects through larger formats, lower-density planning and landscape-led design.

data.title: Hungarian real estate mogul Jellinek questioned in corruption probe
data.description:
Daniel Jellinek, one of Hungary's wealthiest businessmen, was questioned by police and prosecutors on Tuesday as part of an investigation into alleged bribery linked to a bus procurement deal, according to prosecutors and his company.

Hungarian prosecutors said they carried out raids at multiple locations and were questioning four suspects, while three people had been detained. They did not identify any of the suspects or give further details.

After local media reports and comments by Prime Minister Peter Magyar about the case, Indotek Group, the real estate firm that Jellinek heads, told Reuters that Jellinek "was brought in by police for questioning on the morning of September 15."

It said he had voluntarily complied with a summons from Hungary's National Bureau of Investigation on September 10 and had remained continuously available to the authorities since.

According to Forbes' 2025 list of the wealthiest Hungarians, Jellinek was seventh, with estimated assets of about 313 billion forints ($988 million).

He has been involved in several large real estate deals including deals with former premier Viktor Orban's son-in-law Istvan Tiborcz. In 2019 Indotek purchased the iconic Hotel Gellert in Budapest and in 2022 sold it to Tiborcz's BDPST Group.

Indotek said Jellinek, the company's CEO, will continue to cooperate fully with the authorities.

"Our firm position is that Mr. Jellinek has not committed any offence in connection with the matter. We are confident that the investigation will confirm this and that the proceedings against him will soon be discontinued. The investigation does not involve any Indotek Group company or asset, and the Group continues to operate without disruption," the company said.

data.description:
Some 34.9 million passengers travelled through Aena's Spanish airports in August, 4.7% more than in the same month last year, the airport operator said on Tuesday.

Growing passenger numbers highlight Spain's resilience as a tourism hub even as the global airline industry grapples with geopolitical instability, aircraft delivery delays, labour shortages and rising operational costs, which have constrained capacity growth elsewhere.

  • Passenger numbers in the first eight months of 2026 reached 225.5 million, 4.1% higher than a year ago

  • Madrid's Adolfo Suarez Barajas remained the busiest airport in Spain, followed by Josep Tarradellas Barcelona-El Prat and Palma de Mallorca

  • All airports operated by Aena - comprising 46 airports and two heliports in Spain, 17 airports in Brazil, London's Luton and Leeds Bradford - saw a rise of 4.7% to 41.4 million passengers in August
